conviction_note: Small positive lean (p_up 55, abs move 4.0) because the regional peers that reported on 10-15 (PNC, USB, FHN) showed deposit-cost pressure that was real but manageable and traded flat to up pre-market, after KRE had already fallen about 11% from mid-August on exactly that fear. CFG also passed up the chance to warn at Barclays on 09-14, two days before Huntington did, and the Zacks NII consensus (+2.4%) sits just below the bottom of CFG's own +2.5-3.5% guide. Against that: PNC's capital-markets/advisory fees fell 25% q/q, which threatens the consensus of +4% for CFG's fee line, and put skew of +5.5 vol points leans the other way. The findings sum to +0.50 and the scaled number is +0.40; they agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: EPS $1.39 consensus (16 analysts, range $1.32-1.43), revenue $2.34B: https://news.alphastreet.com/citizens-financial-group-cfg-q3-2026-preview-eps-est-1-39-reports-october-16/ and https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/citizens-financial-group-q3fy26-results-eps-seen-1-39-pts-cut/53086897 (2026-10-09). Zacks has $1.38 EPS, NII $1.67B (+2.4% q/q, against a company guide of +2.5-3.5%), non-interest income $656.8M (+1%, matching the guide), capital markets fees $159.1M (+4% q/q) and an ESP of -0.74%: https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:87df5daef094b:0-citizens-financial-is-scheduled-to-post-q3-earnings-what-s-in-store/. Company Q3 guide (Q2 call, 2026-07-16): NII +2.5-3.5%, fees ~+1%, expenses stable to up slightly, NCOs stable to down slightly from 37bp, CET1 ~10.5% with ~$125M of buybacks, Fed assumed on hold; Q4 NIM 3.22-3.27%. Three sources agree on the bar, so no cap applies.
positioning_check: Short interest about 19.2M shares, ~4.5% of float, 4.0 days to cover (Equibles, ~2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/CFG); FINRA 2026-07-15 16.2M shares, 3.0 days (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cfg/short-interest/). Rising but not crowded. I could not find the 2026-09-30 settlement. Baseline: 25-delta skew +5.48 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.66, ATM IV 32.3% against 20-day realised 18%, ATM spread 13.8% of mid. The event-implied move of 6.28% is far above the name's own median reaction of 1.77% (max 7.11%), so the chain is pricing sector stress more than this print. The 20-day run-up is -5.56% and the stock is 14.8% off its 52-week high. In the 9-10 days before the print, four of five sell-side updates were target cuts (UBS 82->77, JPM 78->72.5, MS 90->89, Truist 80->77); Raymond James reinstated at Strong Buy $77.

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-14 (mid-quarter, two days before the Fed hike), CEO Van Saun did not cut any number. He let stand the moderator's framing that full-year NII will exceed the original +10-12%, called the Q4 move into the 3.22-3.27% NIM range 'a pretty big uptick', said 'I wouldn't say spreads are compressing at this point', said a hike adds about 1bp of NIM in Q4 because Citizens is asset-sensitive, and named capital markets 'the star of the show for the next 6 quarters'. Two days later, at the same conference, Huntington cut its 2026 NII growth from 39-43% to ~35% and its 2027 EPS on deposit competition, and fell 5.55%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints with a beat and the guide held both rallied: +4.61% on 2026-07-16 (EPS $1.30 vs $1.25, Q3 NII guide +2.5-3.5%) and +7.11% on 2026-01-21 (baseline). The prints that were in line moved about -0.2% to -1.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The remarks are public, but the stock has fallen about 5.6% over 20 days along with the group (KRE about -11% from mid-August) and the sell-side has cut targets into the print. That treats CFG as if it carried Huntington's deposit-margin problem. If the market had priced CFG's swap-driven NIM path (about 7bp of 2H tailwind from terminated swaps, which is mechanical and not deposit-dependent), CFG would have held up better than the group and the targets would not have been cut. This is a reaffirmation of the company's own guide, so most of the value is a guide held rather than raised, and it is sized small.
findings.independence: Huntington's contrasting cut on 2026-09-16: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/huntington-cut-outlook-fed-hiked-234006771.html. The swap-driven NIM mechanics are from the Q2 call: https://gloom.sh/stocks/cfg/transcripts/q2-2026.

findings.finding: The Street's NII bar is set just under the bottom of CFG's own guide: Zacks consensus NII is $1.67B (+2.4% q/q) against the company's +2.5-3.5% guide. Most of CFG's Q3 NIM expansion is mechanical: management said 2H26 gets about 7bp from terminated swaps plus a couple of basis points of front-book/back-book repricing, about 9bp in total. At Q2 the cumulative interest-bearing deposit beta was 48% and management expected it to stay stable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026, NII up 4.4% against the guide, plus an EPS beat, gave +4.61% (baseline). NII is the line regional banks have traded on this week.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (preview ahead of the 2026-10-16 print; the page shows no date)
findings.why_not_priced: A print at the midpoint of the guide (+3%) would beat a consensus that has been shaded below the guide. If the Street trusted the mechanical swap tailwind, the bar would sit at or above +2.5%. A print inside the company's guide is something the market was told to expect, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: The swap-tailwind figures are from the Q2 call transcript (https://gloom.sh/stocks/cfg/transcripts/q2-2026), a different document from the bar source. The same Q2 call also reports the 48% beta.

findings.finding: Deposit costs rose at the regionals that reported on 10-15. PNC's rate on interest-bearing deposits rose 7bp to 1.98% and its NIM fell 2bp to 2.94%. First Horizon's rose 12bp to 2.45% and its NIM fell 1bp. BofA Securities' regional preview said 'We expect deposit costs to disappoint', citing pricing competition from July through September. CFG's Q3 guide assumed the Fed would hold, and the hike came on 2026-09-16.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nothing CFG-specific: no recent print has missed on NIM. Among peers on 10-15, PNC (NIM -2bp) was +0.66% pre-market and FHN (NIM -1bp) +3.07% pre-market, so the margin dip was not punished.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: KRE is about -11% from mid-August and BofA's note is public. CFG's deposit base has run a 48% beta, so a peer-sized rise of 5-12bp would cut into a NIM expansion the Street models at about +4-5bp for Q3. This is a peer proxy, not CFG's own number, so it is sized small, and the peer stock reactions argue the market has already absorbed it.
findings.independence: First Horizon Q3 call, 2026-10-15: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-first-horizon-tops-eps-view-in-q3-2026-as-shares-rise-93CH-4952231. BofA note via American Banker, 2026-10-09: https://www.americanbanker.com/news/the-impact-of-higher-rates-will-dominate-banks-3q-earnings. Against it: USB's NIM rose 5bp (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-bancorp-q3-2026-slides-record-revenue-raised-guidance-93CH-5635673).

findings.finding: PNC's capital markets and advisory revenue (it owns Harris Williams, the closest public read on middle-market M&A advisory) fell 25% q/q to $433M in Q3 2026, flat year on year. JPMorgan's CFO said dealmaking slowed in late September, with deals delayed rather than cancelled. WTW counts mid-sized deals as flat to softer while mega deals carried value. The consensus for CFG's capital markets fees is $159.1M, +4% q/q, after a record Q2 that was up 14% q/q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fee income, led by capital markets, drove the Q2 2026 beat (+4.61%). In July, CFG's Ted Swimmer said he expected M&A to pick up 'into the fourth quarter and into next year' and not in Q3. PNC guided Q4 capital markets +15% and its stock was +0.66% pre-market despite the -25% q/q.
findings.why_not_priced: The Zacks line consensus still has CFG capital markets rising 4% q/q off a record Q2. If the PNC read-through were priced, that line would have been revised to flat or down. Net of the rest of the company: capital markets is about 7% of revenue, so a 15% miss on the line is about $24M pre-tax, roughly $0.04 of EPS (~3% of the bar), and NII (about 72% of revenue) would have to come in at the top of its guide to cover it. The likely Q4 fee guide-up (PNC +15%) softens the reaction, which is why this is sized below the EPS arithmetic.
findings.independence: JPM CFO comment via Fortune and Investing.com, 2026-10-15: https://ph.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/bank-earnings-scorecard-winners-and-misses-across-two-days-of-results-93CH-2629025. WTW Q3 2026 deal counts: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/08/3377298/0/en/global-m-a-market-hits-new-high-as-bigger-deals-dominate.html. Against it: Goldman posted record advisory fees.

findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-14 Van Saun said Q3 loan growth 'won't be as significant as what we had in Q2', so earning-asset growth, the other leg of the +2.5-3.5% NII guide, is softer than the Q2 run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate history; loan growth is part of the NII line, see the second finding.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is public and the NII consensus already sits below the guide. Its residual value is that it limits the NII upside in the second finding. PNC's half-of-quarter loan growth landed in the last two weeks, which suggests late-quarter demand could offset it.
findings.independence: Same document as the first finding. It is the negative half of that document and is kept separate because it lands on a different line.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: KRE is about -11% from its mid-August high, XLF fell about 4% after the 09-16 hike while the S&P rose 1.6%, CFG is -5.6% over 20 days, and four of five sell-side target moves since 09-23 were cuts. The regionals that reported on 10-15 then traded up on prints showing modest margin pressure (PNC +0.66% pre-market, USB +2.04% pre-market with NIM +5bp and raised full-year guidance, FHN +3.07% pre-market), unlike the megabanks on 10-13/14 (C -5.6%, WFC about -3%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CFG rose on the last two prints that were better than feared (+4.61%, +7.11%). Peer reactions on 10-15 are the closest analogue.
findings.why_not_priced: Skew of +5.48 vol points says the option market is paying for downside, which is the deposit-cost fear. This finding argues that fear is overpriced for CFG because its NIM path is swap-driven and the regional peers were not sold on the same issue. This is a sign against the skew; the reason given is that the 10-15 regional prints were bought, not sold. It is sized below what the first-day peer moves alone would suggest, because pre-market prices are not closes.
findings.independence: Peer pre-market moves: PNC https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-pnc-beats-q3-2026-profit-view-as-revenue-slips-93CH-5635740, FHN https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-first-horizon-tops-eps-view-in-q3-2026-as-shares-rise-93CH-4952231, USB https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-bancorp-q3-2026-slides-record-revenue-raised-guidance-93CH-5635673. Target cuts: https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/citizens-financial-group-q3fy26-results-eps-seen-1-39-pts-cut/53086897. This shares the PNC document with the third finding, read for the stock reaction rather than the margin.

findings.finding: Van Saun said at Barclays that CET1 has 'generally' run at 10.6-10.7%, above the 10-10.5% operating range, and could 'run closer towards 10%' over time. Against the Q3 guide of ~10.5% with ~$125M of buybacks, that leaves room for a larger Q4 buyback guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable; buybacks were $225M in Q2 and $920M returned in total over 1H26.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus capital path follows the guided ~10.5% CET1 and $125M of Q3 buybacks. A step-up in the Q4 buyback guide would be new. It is small relative to a $27B market cap.
findings.independence: Q2 call for the guided CET1 and buyback: https://www.webull.com/news/15238011352409088. This shares the Barclays document with the first and fifth findings.

findings.finding: CFG redeemed all of its 4.000% fixed-rate reset Series G non-cumulative perpetual preferred on 2026-10-06 (8-K, items 5.03 and 9.01), at its first reset date. After the September hike that coupon would otherwise have reset materially higher.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small to price: it removes preferred dividends that would have reset upward, with a slight Tier 1 capital cost. The money pays down a security that was about to get more expensive, so the sign is neutral to slightly positive. The 8-K gives no redemption amount.

findings.finding: A data-breach matter from a third-party vendor: Citizens filed with the Massachusetts AG on 2026-04-28 and a second notice dated 2026-08-10 covers payment-card data accessed in spring 2026. Class actions seek more than $5M per complaint.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial to a bank of $234B in assets unless a litigation reserve appears in the quarter. Nothing suggests it has.

baseline_tension: The sign cuts against the +5.48 put skew but agrees with the -5.6% 20-day run-up being sector fear rather than CFG news. The positive lean rests on regional peers being bought on 10-15, which is why p_up stops at 55.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, inside the guide: the Barclays reaffirmation and the NII-bar-below-guide findings both land inside what CFG already guided, so they move toward 0 (+0.6 to +0.4, +0.5 to +0.3).

Rule 7, sign against the skew: the positioning finding goes long against +5.48 put skew. I kept the stated reason (regional peers bought on 10-15) and trimmed it from +0.8 to +0.6. p_up went from 56 to 55.

Rules 5 and 9, proxy, segment and own caveat: the PNC capital-markets read-through is a peer proxy on about 7% of revenue, and PNC's Q4 +15% guide softens it, so -0.7 to -0.5. The deposit-cost proxy's own text says peers were not punished for it, so -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 1, reaction history: CFG bought its last two beats (+4.6%, +7.1%), so beat-related sizes were not damped. abs_move_pct is unchanged at 4.0.
